name: 7049-decodeheavy-8b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one in-process vLLM engine.
architecture: LlamaForCausalLM, 8.03B params, bf16 checkpoint, 8 KV heads x head_dim 128 = 128 KiB of KV per token, 131072-token window; the rest is in the checkpoint's config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=256, warmup the first 25% by completion, max_requests 1334 leaving 1000 measured, 900 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix buckets. Prompt exactly 128 tokens, output exactly 256 (the backend sets `ignore_eos=True`), n=1, no best_of, sampling at engine defaults; the chat template makes the ENGINE's prompt count read a little above 128, which nothing here reads.
purpose: An eight-billion-parameter chat assistant writing long replies to short prompts for 256 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# ENGINE: commit 015e6cc252450920411a6779fbb9e631c3698de1 (v0.5.5 era). An unknown key is a
# TypeError when the engine args are constructed, so do not add keys from a later vLLM.
# Interpreter and hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml, which is NOT portable.

model: NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct

# Online dynamic FP8 of the bf16 checkpoint at load; no FP8 checkpoint is downloaded.
quantization: fp8

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# Equals what `auto` resolves to for this checkpoint; pinned so a future default cannot drift it.
dtype: bfloat16

# DO NOT RAISE: with the declared 256 streams and 256 output tokens this is what keeps the KV pool
# clear of exhaustion.
max-num-seqs: 256

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enforce-eager: false
enable-prefix-caching: false
